A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAD-Tokenizer work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-C support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAD generation and editing experiments, human evaluations, tokenizer and decoding ablations, and supplementary analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1-4 and 7, together with qualitative results and failure analyses. Retained results qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an embedding-space squared-error term to the stated adapter-alignment loss, beyond v1's reconstruction of VQ latent vectors. This locally revises the training objective; primitive pooling, instruction tuning and FSA decoding otherwise retain their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use SkexGen-derived data and the CADFusion and CAD-Editor datasets for the same text-to-CAD generation and editing tasks. The appendix examples introduce no changed task or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain CAD-Editor, CADFusion, GPT-4o and Vanilla-LLaMA, along with HNC-CAD, BPE, tokenizer variants, top-p sampling and beam search in their respective ablations. Newly cited CAD methods are not added to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported backbone and source of frozen embedding/logit layers from LLaMA-3-8b-Instruct to LLaMA-3-8b. Splits, sample counts, training budgets, metrics and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged. This is a revised setting specification; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The tokenizer reconstruction/compression studies, tokenizer integration and decoding ablations, distributional-metric analysis, qualitative examples and failure cases are retained. Calling Tables 2-4 ablation studies in their revised captions adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimates. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The reported entries and numerical values in Tables 1-4 and 7 are unchanged, as are the compression plot and qualitative results. For example, CAD-Tokenizer's editing F1 scores remain 88.6 and 94.8. The revised backbone specification does not establish a performance gain or loss.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 substantively revises the mathematical definition of the alignment loss by adding the embedding-space reconstruction term. Other mathematical objectives and CAD definitions are retained; no theorem, proof or formal guarantee is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified text-based CAD prototyping, primitive-aware tokenization, LLM alignment, FSA decoding, and improvements in quality and efficiency. The scope of the principal contributions is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains that the additional alignment-loss term ensures both adapters are trained and explicitly identifies the FSA map as specific to its CAD representation in Figure 3's caption. Existing result interpretations, dataset and metric limitations, and failure-case explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The backbone identifier is revised in Section 4.1, and Algorithm 1 clarifies sequence extension by replacing Seq.insert(choice) with Seq.append(choice). Other hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing details and evaluation prompts are retained. Moving the FSA specification does not itself add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations to Cadmium, CAD-Coder, CAD-GPT and CAD-MLLM and refines the distinction from earlier CAD encoders and codebook-based systems. This modestly updates related-work coverage without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes local grammar edits, explains previously unexplained loss symbols, revises part of the related-work discussion, and adds an LLM-use statement and acknowledgments. Author/header text also changes. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 and the FSA diagram move into the main text, with v1 Figure 8 becoming v2 Figure 3. Table 7 is repositioned, Tables 2-4 receive revised captions, and conference headers and page reflow alter the layout. The existing visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical clarity by expanding the alignment objective and explaining how its terms train both adapters, defining loss symbols, and bringing the existing FSA specification into the main discussion. Added related-work citations provide useful context. These are limited gains: empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not explain whether the revised backbone specification reflects a correction or new training.
